description: Fig. 9 is a ten-panel composite figure that mixes transmission electron microscopy of the impact-fracture deformation zone with fracture-mechanism schematics. (a) and (c) are bright-field TEM micrographs of R650 with 1 µm scale bars, showing dark rounded carbide particles (encircled by white dashed lines) inside a lamellar ferrite matrix, with dislocations blocked and piled up in the regions adjacent to the carbides. (b) and (d) are HRTEM images with 5 nm scale bars; a red dashed square marks the ferrite/carbide boundary and the inset is an IFFT-filtered lattice image annotated "Atomic Shear" (yellow dashed ellipse) and "Dislocation" (red line). (e) and (h) are schematics of the impact fracture for R650, (f) and (i) for R750, (g) and (j) for R850/R950. (e, f) show black carbides within lamellae labelled δ-F, F and Carbide; (e) contains numerous fine carbides whereas (f) has fewer, coarser particles. (g) is carbide-free, showing only outlined equiaxed grains labelled DIF embedded in M (martensite) within δ-F lamellae. In the lower row a grey wedge representing the crack is blunted and branched in (h, i) but propagates straight through in (j). Small inset photographs of the fractured specimen appear at bottom right of (h–j). No numeric axis values are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (c) are TEM micrographs of the impact-fractured deformation zone of R650 with 1 µm scale bars; dark rounded particles (carbides) are highlighted with white dashed circles and curved dislocation lines concentrate in the matrix next to them.
Panels (b) and (d) are HRTEM images with 5 nm scale bars; each has a red dashed square on the carbide/ferrite boundary that is expanded into an inset IFFT-filtered lattice image.

The IFFT insets in (b) and (d) carry the printed annotations "Atomic Shear" (yellow dashed ellipse) and "Dislocation" (red marking), identifying localised shear and dislocation cores at the ferrite/carbide interface.
The caption assigns (a, c) to TEM and (b, d) to HRTEM and IFFT of selected carbide regions for R650, and assigns the schematics (e, h) to R650, (f, i) to R750 and (g, j) to R850/R950.
In the schematics the printed phase labels are δ-F, F, Carbide (e), and δ-F, DIF, M (g).

Schematic (e) shows a dense population of fine black carbide particles in the ferrite lamellae, whereas (f) shows markedly fewer and coarser black particles, consistent with decreasing carbide content and coarsening at higher rolling temperature.
Schematic (g) contains no carbide symbols at all; instead outlined equiaxed grains labelled DIF sit within M lamellae bounded by δ-F bands.

In (h) and (i) the grey wedge representing the crack is blunted and split into multiple branches along the lamellar boundaries, while in (j) the same wedge continues as a single straight path through the carbide-free structure.
Small inset photographs of the fractured impact specimen are placed at the bottom right of panels (h), (i) and (j); they are too small to resolve detail.
The citing text states that after impact deformation numerous dislocations were blocked by carbides and piled up in the regions adjacent to carbides (Fig. 9a and c).
The citing text states that when the carbide diameter exceeds 10 nm, numerous dislocations and atomic shearing are observed at the ferrite/carbide boundaries, attributed to the Orowan mechanism.
The citing text states that the impact absorption energy of R750 decreased by approximately 60 % compared with R650, and that for R850/R950 it falls below 10 J.

The citing text describes the R650 fracture mode as mixed: crack blunting hinders propagation perpendicular to the lamellae while lamellar separation and secondary defects guide cracks along the separation direction.
No numeric values (axis ticks, energy values, particle diameters, temperatures) are printed anywhere on the panels themselves; all numbers in the surrounding text are not confirmable from the pixels.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the impact-fractured deformation zone of R650, 1 µm scale bar; dark rounded carbide particles in a lighter lamellar matrix, one carbide marked with a white dashed circle, dislocations accumulating adjacent to it.

HRTEM image of a carbide region (5 nm scale bar) with a red dashed square marking the ferrite/carbide boundary; inset IFFT-filtered image annotated "Atomic Shear" (yellow dashed) and "Dislocation" (red).
Second bright-field TEM micrograph of the R650 deformation zone, 1 µm scale bar; lamellar ferrite/carbide structure with a white dashed circle marking a carbide and dislocation tangles nearby.
HRTEM image of a carbide/ferrite boundary (5 nm scale bar) with a red dashed box and inset IFFT image showing lattice fringes with an annotated defective/sheared region.
Schematic of R650 lamellar structure before/at fracture: many small black carbide particles distributed in lamellae labelled δ-F, F and Carbide.
Schematic of R750 lamellar structure: same lamellar architecture but noticeably fewer and larger black carbide particles.
Schematic of R850/R950 structure labelled δ-F: no carbides, only outlined equiaxed grains labelled DIF inside M (martensite) lamellae.

Schematic of R650 impact fracture: a grey wedge (crack) enters the carbide-containing laminate, is blunted and branches along lamellar boundaries; small photograph inset of the fractured specimen at bottom right.
Schematic of R750 impact fracture: grey wedge crack in a structure with coarse, sparse carbides, showing straighter propagation and lamellar separation; small specimen photograph inset.
Schematic of R850/R950 impact fracture: grey wedge crack propagates straight through the carbide-free honeycomb structure with no blunting or deflection; small specimen photograph inset.
